note: Taiwan's largest card issuers are CTBC, Cathay United, E.SUN and Taishin. CTBC's card pages answer with a script-only holding page (status 202), Cathay United's serve only a script shell, and E.SUN's answer a captcha, which this research doesn't pass (2026-10-30); so Taishin Bank is written, with Standard Chartered Taiwan, whose fee sheet this file has held since 2026-10-29. Standard Chartered Taiwan's card fees and interest (版號 2026 年 8 月, read again 2026-10-30): each tier's principal-card annual fee, the first year free on every card (written; until now this file left it out): classic 1,200, gold 1,800, platinum 2,400, Signature (the cash-back 御璽卡) 3,600, the 昇利卡 5,000, World 5,000, Infinite 10,000 and Beyond 30,000 Taiwan dollars, the next year's fee waived by spending 12,000 (classic and gold), 24,000 (platinum, Signature, 昇利卡), 120,000 (World) or 360,000 (Infinite) in a year, or by 12 or 24 transactions, which the game doesn't count. The sheet gives the classic, gold and platinum waiver only to the H card, Combo card, Rewards instalment card and the former Hsinchu bank's cards, so the other classic, gold and platinum cards (渣打信用卡) are written without it; the 渣打信用卡 普卡 this file held is kept, its spending waiver removed for that reason. The LINE Bank co-brand card costs 2,400 (its next-year waiver for e-statements isn't written); the Chunghwa Post card 300, 600 or 1,200 by tier, the first year free (the balance-transfer versions' higher fees aren't written). Revolving interest is at most 15% a year, the holders priced in four tiers (7.9%, 9.9%, 12.9%, 14.98% as of May 2026), written as 7.9% to 14.98%; a cash advance costs 3.5% plus 100 dollars (3.5% alone on the LINE Bank card); spending in another currency 1.5% (1% to the card network and 0.5% to the bank); a late payment 300 dollars the first month (400 and 500 in the next two running, and nothing on an overdue amount of 1,000 or less, neither written). Taishin Bank's card rates and fees disclosure (2026/01/02, read 2026-10-30) and its notice of the annual fees in force from 1 September 2025 (posted 2025/07/01): the principal card's annual fee by type, from 300 for a classic or gold card to 30,000 for the 環球無限卡, the Cathay Pacific titanium card free; the cards the notice groups with its business cards (the dual-currency, JKOPAY, Gogoro, Flygo and Rose cards) cost 4,500, and the business and Woojii World business cards aren't written. Its waivers, which the notice says are posted on the bank's site, weren't read and aren't written. Revolving interest runs 2.88% to 15% a year by the bank's credit score; a cash advance costs 3.5% plus 150 dollars; spending in another currency 1.5% (1% plus 0.5%); a late payment 300 dollars (400 and 500 in the next two running). Both banks' minimum payment is 10% of the period's new purchases plus 5% (Taishin) or all (Standard Chartered) of other parts, at least 1,000 dollars, a sum of parts the form doesn't hold, so it isn't written; neither states a grace period. Wave 4 (2026-10-30): Taipei Fubon Bank (台北富邦銀行), one of the largest card issuers, is added in place of CTBC, Cathay United and E.SUN (see above), First Bank's card site answering 403 and Hua Nan's not answering (2026-10-30). Its card fee statement (台北富邦銀行信用卡主要費用說明, 版本日期 202608, read 2026-10-30): revolving interest is the bank's index-linked mortgage base rate plus a margin of 4.75% to 13.91% by credit score, capped at 15% a year; the base rate isn't on the statement, so the cap is written, as 15% a year, with no lower end. The principal card's annual fee by tier: ordinary 800, gold 1,200, platinum 1,500, titanium, Signature and 晶緻 1,800, World and Infinite 5,000, 尊御世界卡 (World Elite) 10,000 dollars (the business card's 3,000 isn't written); every tier but the World Elite has its first year free, and the next year's fee is waived by spending 360,000 (World and Infinite), 60,000 or 12 transactions (titanium tier; the count isn't written) or 2,400 dollars (platinum, gold, ordinary) in a year, written as spending over the fee's year; the World Elite's waivers depend on the holder's wealth-management membership and aren't written. A cash advance costs 3.5% plus 150 dollars; a late payment 300 dollars the first month (400 and 500 in the next two running, and nothing on 1,000 dollars or less unpaid, neither written); a returned cheque 300 dollars. Spending in another currency carries the card network's fee, whose figure the statement doesn't give, and the bank's 0.5%; only the 0.5% is written. The minimum payment is a sum of parts (10% of the period's new purchases, 5% of the rest, and others, at least 800 dollars), which the form doesn't hold, and isn't written; no grace period is stated.
